root_cause.text: The ICMP/ICMPv6 error delivery path incorrectly allowed encapsulated packets with inner protocol IPPROTO_RAW to be matched and delivered to raw sockets, even though IPPROTO_RAW sockets are send-only and must not receive packets.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit checks in `icmp_socket_deliver()` and `icmpv6_notify()` to drop packets when `protocol == IPPROTO_RAW` / `nexthdr == IPPROTO_RAW`, and the commit/CVE states that a malicious ICMP packet can set the inner protocol field to 255 and match `socket(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 255)`, leading to FNHE cache changes despite `man 7 raw` saying “Receiving of all IP protocols via IPPROTO_RAW is not possible using raw sockets.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent ICMP error delivery to IPPROTO_RAW sockets by dropping those packets through the existing error path and accounting them as input errors.
intent_record.what: The function changed its early pskb_may_pull() failure return into a goto to a new out: label, added a new conditional that jumps to out when protocol == IPPROTO_RAW, kept the raw_icmp_error() and protocol err_handler path unchanged for other protocols, inserted an explicit return after the normal handling path, and moved __ICMP_INC_STATS(..., ICMP_MIB_INERRORS) into the shared out: block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ICMP socket delivery now treats IPPROTO_RAW packets as an error case and stops before calling raw_icmp_error() or any protocol-specific err_handler for them, while still incrementing ICMP_MIB_INERRORS just like the existing malformed-packet path. Normal processing for other protocols is unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early guard in icmpv6_notify() to stop processing raw IPv6 next-header packets and return a generic drop reason.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added in icmpv6_notify() after the existing early-drop check to test whether nexthdr equals IPPROTO_RAW; if so, it sets reason to SKB_DROP_REASON_NOT_SPECIFIED and jumps to the out label.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packets reaching this path with a next-header value of IPPROTO_RAW now exit early instead of continuing into the later ICMPv6 notification handling logic, preventing further processing of that unsupported/unhandled protocol case while recording a generic drop reason.

The change directly blocks ICMPv6 error processing for encapsulated packets whose inner next-header/protocol is raw, preventing delivery to raw sockets. This matches the root cause that IPPROTO_RAW packets were incorrectly allowed through the ICMP/ICMPv6 error path.

candidates.rationale: This directly delivers ICMP errors to raw sockets for the inner protocol without excluding IPPROTO_RAW, causing send-only raw sockets to receive encapsulated error packets.
This looks up the protocol handler for the encapsulated protocol and enables further error delivery based solely on protocol number, with no guard against IPPROTO_RAW.
This condition allows invoking protocol-specific error handling for the inner protocol without filtering out IPPROTO_RAW, contributing to invalid receive-side processing.
This actually dispatches the ICMP error to the matched protocol error handler for the inner protocol, again without excluding IPPROTO_RAW.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement delivers ICMP errors to raw sockets based on the inner protocol value. Without excluding IPPROTO_RAW, it incorrectly allows send-only IPPROTO_RAW sockets to receive encapsulated error packets, which is the root cause described.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code is sufficient because it contains the full socket-delivery logic relevant to the root cause. The new helper `icmp_socket_deliver()` does `const struct iphdr *iph = (const struct iphdr *) skb->data;` and then `int protocol = iph->protocol;`, followed by `raw_icmp_error(skb, protocol, info);`. There is no check excluding `IPPROTO_RAW` before delivering the ICMP error to raw sockets. Since the vulnerability is that encapsulated packets with inner protocol `IPPROTO_RAW` were incorrectly matched and delivered to raw sockets, this helper still contains the vulnerable construct: it unconditionally uses the inner IP header protocol and passes it to raw socket error delivery. The subsequent `ipprot = rcu_dereference(inet_protos[protocol]); if (ipprot && ipprot->err_handler) ipprot->err_handler(skb, info);` also lacks any special handling for `IPPROTO_RAW`. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present, and the fix is not yet present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function is sufficient because it contains the ICMP error delivery path and the protocol demux lookup relevant to the described root cause. In this version, after parsing the inner packet protocol into `protocol`, the code does `raw_icmp_error(skb, protocol, info);` and then indexes the protocol table directly with `ipprot = rcu_dereference(inet_protos[protocol]);`. The commit only changes the lookup from `inet_protos[hash]` to `inet_protos[protocol]` after removing `hash = protocol & (MAX_INET_PROTOS - 1);`. There is no check excluding `IPPROTO_RAW` before delivering the ICMP error to raw sockets or before protocol demux. Since the root cause is that encapsulated packets with inner protocol `IPPROTO_RAW` were incorrectly allowed to match and be delivered to raw sockets, and this function still calls `raw_icmp_error()` for any `protocol` without filtering out `IPPROTO_RAW`, the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present because there is no conditional such as rejecting or skipping `IPPROTO_RAW` in this error delivery path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `icmp_unreach()`. After extracting the inner IP header and protocol (`protocol = iph->protocol;`), the code unconditionally delivers the ICMP error to raw sockets based on that inner protocol: `hash = protocol & (MAX_INET_PROTOS - 1);` followed by `while ((raw_sk = __raw_v4_lookup(raw_sk, protocol, iph->daddr, iph->saddr, skb->dev->ifindex)) != NULL) { raw_err(raw_sk, skb, info); ... }`. There is no check excluding `IPPROTO_RAW` before looking up and notifying raw sockets. The vulnerability root cause is exactly this missing exclusion: encapsulated packets with inner protocol `IPPROTO_RAW` must not be matched/delivered because `IPPROTO_RAW` sockets are send-only. Since the function still performs raw socket delivery for whatever `iph->protocol` contains, including `IPPROTO_RAW`, the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
